contract.note: the intake contract reads raw, unit, number, street, suburb, size_class and barcode out of a label; the scanner is address-only (V4 section 10.2), so the sender, the names, the phone numbers and the marketing are distractors and are annotated, not scored

fields.acceptance: the number, the street and the suburb must all equal the gold after normalisation; a transposed number is a miss; a wrong block is a miss whatever the string is
equal to the gold after normalisation; a suburb from the sender block is a miss
equal to the gold after normalisation; a missing unit on a label that has one is a miss; a label without a unit is scored as "no unit", not as a miss

fields.example: Kea Outdoor / 12 Madras Street / Christchurch Central
fields.acceptance: not scored: the scanner is address-only (V4 section 10.2). The sender block is the wrong-block distractor, so it is annotated, never read
not scored: the product returns the delivery address, never the name. The block is annotated so the classifier has to find it

fields.expected_format: the carrier barcode, linear or 2D, with the human-readable form under it
fields.acceptance: the decoded payload must equal the gold; a 2D symbol must decode to the same payload as the human-readable form; a missing decode is a miss
the same calendar day; a missing field is a miss
fields.source: the printed despatch or print date

fields.expected_format: the carrier tracking or ticket number
fields.acceptance: equal to the gold after normalisation
the same weight in kilograms; a missing field is a miss
the flag is present or it is not; a label without the flag is scored as "not fragile", not as a miss

lines: <unit> - optional, printed on its own line above the street line (Unit 6, Flat 6, 6/12)
<number>[suffix] <street name> <street type> - the street line (42B Main North Road)
address_format.note: the shape the address engine in packages/nz-address parses; the street type is compared on the long form (the table in packages/nz-address/src/constants.ts), a macron is significant, and the suburb is never guessed from the street name
address_format.source: the NZ Post labelling standards ask for one block of text, left aligned, with the sender and the receiver marked (To and From); the shape above is the shape our own parser reads

global: collapse the runs of whitespace into one space
strip the leading and trailing punctuation
never change a macron: the Maori place names are significant
normalisation.street_types: the street type is compared on the long form, using the table in packages/nz-address/src/constants.ts (Rd is Road, St is Street, Tce is Terrace and so on)
normalisation.unit: the words unit, flat, apartment and apt are dropped; the number is what is compared
normalisation.date: the printed date is parsed and compared as an ISO calendar day
normalisation.weight: the printed weight is parsed and compared in kilograms
normalisation.tracking_and_barcode: the whitespace is stripped and the text is upper-cased

acceptance.address: the address counts as read when the number, the street and the suburb all equal the gold after the normalisation, and the block that was read is the recipient block
acceptance.wrong_block: a read of the sender block, of the marketing or of the barcode text is a wrong-block failure, whatever the string is; the sender block looks exactly like an address, which is the point of the slice
acceptance.unit: a label without a unit is scored as "no unit"; a label with a unit and no unit read is a miss
acceptance.barcode: the decoded payload has to equal the gold; a 2D symbol that decodes to the same payload as the human-readable form counts as read
acceptance.partial: a field that is on the label but was not read is a miss for that field; it never makes the address read
acceptance.no_guessing: a field that cannot be read is null, never a guess (the same rule as the intake contract)

label_types.name: Thermal label
label_types.look: printed on a thermal printer: the letters are dark on a warm off-white paper, the edges of the letters are soft, and the print fades to pale grey after a week in the sun

label_types.name: Laser-printed label
label_types.look: printed on a laser printer: crisp letter edges, a true black toner on a white background, no dot pattern, and the toner cracks where the paper has been folded, so a crease through a line of text leaves that line unreadable
label_types.note: the reprint from a desktop printer and the courier own stationery

label_types.name: Handwritten docket
label_types.look: written by the courier in ballpoint: uneven baselines, the letters joined, the pen pressure changing across a line
label_types.note: the synthetic ones are drawn in a script font with a per-character jitter; they are not scans of handwriting

label_types.name: Sticker
label_types.look: a small adhesive label: a thin die-cut border, a small print area, often rubbed at one corner where it was pulled off a parcel
label_types.note: the pouch sticker and the small ticket
